title: Sole Proprietorship Structure and Liability
context: Analyze the defining features of a sole proprietorship as a form of business ownership. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A sole proprietorship is owned by one person who also manages and runs the business.
The sole proprietorship is not a legal entity of its own, so profits are reported on the owner's personal income tax statement.
A sole proprietor enjoys limited liability so private assets stay fully protected if business debts cannot be repaid.
Sole proprietorships require substantial minimum share capital before trading may begin.
Hiring staff removes the sole proprietor from responsibility for major management decisions and business risk.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Check the sentence against the core concept named in the stem, including every scope word.

Ownership and day-to-day management rest with a single proprietor.

The statement is true.
TRUE — Check the sentence against the core concept named in the stem, including every scope word.

Without separate legal personality, profits are taxed as the owner's personal income.

The statement is true.
FALSE — Read the quantifier. Words such as never, always, only, or all turn a generally valid idea into a claim that one counterexample rejects.

The sole proprietor has unlimited liability; private assets are also at stake.

The statement is false. A student who overlooked the word "cannot" in "A sole proprietor enjoys limited liability so private assets stay fully protected if business…" would treat the restriction as absent and mark the statement true.
FALSE — Check the sentence against the core concept named in the stem, including every scope word.

Sole proprietorships are easy to establish and face no such capital requirement.

The statement is false. A student who matched the topic to "Sole proprietorships require substantial minimum share capital before trading may begin" without checking the rest of the sentence would mark the statement true.
FALSE — Check the sentence against the core concept named in the stem, including every scope word.

Even with hired personnel, the proprietor retains key decisions and bears the risk.

The statement is false. A student who matched the topic to "Hiring staff removes the sole proprietor from responsibility for major management decisions and business…" without checking the rest of the sentence would mark the statement true.

title: Partnership Agreement and Partner Liability
context: Consider two consultants who jointly found a business and draft a partnership agreement covering ownership shares, profit division, and decision rights. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A partnership is formed when two or more persons jointly found a business and settle rights in a partnership agreement.
In a general partnership all partners typically share equal rights, liabilities, and responsibilities.
Each general partner is solely liable for all debts of the business under unlimited liability.
A limited partner who does not manage the business still carries unlimited liability for all partnership debts.
Partners cannot specialise in different tasks because every partner must perform identical management duties.
tactical_explanations:
TRUE — Map the scenario onto the textbook category first, then test whether the sentence describes that category accurately.

Joint founding plus a partnership agreement defines the partnership structure.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Read the quantifier. Words such as never, always, only, or all turn a generally valid idea into a claim that one counterexample rejects.

General partnerships assign equal rights, liabilities, and responsibilities to partners.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Read the quantifier. Words such as never, always, only, or all turn a generally valid idea into a claim that one counterexample rejects.

Unlimited liability means each general partner can be held for the whole debt.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Read the quantifier. Words such as never, always, only, or all turn a generally valid idea into a claim that one counterexample rejects.

In a limited partnership, a limited partner's liability is capped at the capital contributed.

The statement is false. A student who overlooked the word "all" in "A limited partner who does not manage the business still carries unlimited liability for…" would treat the restriction as absent and mark the statement true.

FALSE — Read the quantifier. Words such as never, always, only, or all turn a generally valid idea into a claim that one counterexample rejects.

Partners may share tasks and specialise while remaining jointly responsible.

The statement is false. A student who overlooked the word "cannot" in "Partners cannot specialise in different tasks because every partner must perform identical management duties" would treat the restriction as absent and mark the statement true.

title: Corporations as Legal Entities

Shareholders need not manage the corporation, and managers need not own shares of the business.
Shareholders' liability is usually limited to the amount they invested when buying the shares.
Share capital is divided into shares so that large sums can be raised when investors purchase stock.
Once share prices rise on the stock exchange after issue, the issuing corporation automatically receives additional financing equal to that price rise.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Check the sentence against the core concept named in the stem, including every scope word.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Map the scenario onto the textbook category first, then test whether the sentence describes that category accurately.

The statement is true.

TRUE — Map the scenario onto the textbook category first, then test whether the sentence describes that category accurately.

The statement is true.

FALSE — Read the quantifier. Words such as never, always, only, or all turn a generally valid idea into a claim that one counterexample rejects.

title: Matching Finance to Use Cost and Gearing

A highly geared business may struggle to raise further credit except at higher interest rates and/or against additional collateral.
When loan capital is already high, internal funds or new equity investors can reduce insolvency risk relative to taking another large loan.
The only relevant criterion when choosing a source of finance is the absolute interest rate, so matching term to asset life and gearing risk can be ignored.
